mainTopic: ספק דרוסה: the רב–שמואל dispute and שמואל's birds, then the rules for checking a clawed animal, the סימנים, and rotten flesh
overview: The גמרא pinpoints where רב and שמואל disagree about ספק דרוסה: the predator is quiet while the birds cry out. אמימר rules like שמואל that we must worry. The גמרא suggests רב may have retracted, but rejects that proof: רב sent the birds to שמואל only because it was שמואל's town. The גמרא then explains each detail of how שמואל destroyed the birds, ending with the river, which made the איסור public. רב אשי rules that a duck bloodied among reeds is permitted, since we assume a reed hurt it rather than a cat. Several rulings follow on how to check a דרוסה: near the intestines, across the whole body cavity, and even at the סימנים. Other rulings say detached סימנים need רוב, and rotten flesh counts as missing, so a crumbling lung is טרפה. רב נחמן and רב זביד compare clawing with a thorn wound and with the סימנים. The amud ends as a new question from רב ביבי בר אביי begins.

steps.title: Where exactly רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pinpoints the case of the מחלוקת: the predator is silent while the birds are clucking.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...each other. They disagree when the predator is quiet and the birds are clucking. One Sage holds the predator is doing something to them, and the other holds the birds are only clucking out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the case where רב and שמואל argue about a doubtful clawing. It says the argument is only when the predator is quiet and the birds are noisy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both were noisy, everyone agrees they were just frightening each other. When only the birds cry out, שמואל reads it as a sign of clawing, so there is real worry. רב says fear alone can explain the noise, so there is no worry.

keyTerms.meaning: they (the birds) are clucking or crying out

phrases.english: each other.
Where they disagree
is when it is quiet
and they are clucking.
One Sage holds
phrases.notes: This first 'Sage' is שמואל, and the second one is רב.

phrases.english: it is doing something to them,
and the other Sage holds
because of their fear of it
is why they are doing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי דְּאִיהוּ קָא שָׁתֵיק וְאִינְהוּ קָמְקַרְקְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier definition of the רב and שמואל dispute that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only when the predator is silent and the birds cry out. שמואל sees this as a sign of clawing, and רב attributes it to fear.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: חוששין לספק דרוסה (we worry). רב: we don't worry, because the noise could just be fear.

steps.title: אמימר rules that we worry about a doubtful clawing
steps.stepSummary: אמימר decides the הלכה is to be concerned about ספק דרוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that we are concerned about a doubtful clawing.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives the practical ruling: we must worry when it is unclear whether the animal was clawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the strict view, which matches שמואל. It sets up the next question about what happens to רב's lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned, we take the doubt seriously
a doubt whether an animal was clawed by a predator (which would make it a טריפה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halachic bottom line for a doubtful clawing.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
The halakha is that we are concerned
about an uncertain clawing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הִלְכְתָא חוֹשְׁשִׁין לִסְפֵק דְּרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute just defined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is like שמואל: we are concerned about ספק דרוסה.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: what about רב's view?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר's ruling by pointing to רב's lenient statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What about this statement of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר how he can rule strictly when the great אמורא רב said we need not worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Although the line is worded as a question, it works as a challenge. רב's opinion carries great weight, so a ruling against it needs an explanation.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What about this statement of Rav?
phrases.notes: He means רב's view that we don't worry about a doubtful clawing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: הַאי דְּרַב מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that we are concerned about ספק דרוסה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב said we need not be concerned, so how can the הלכה ignore him?

steps.title: אמימר: I don't hold like רב
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he does not accept רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear it. That is to say, I do not hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers politely that he 'did not hear' רב's view, and the גמרא explains that this means he does not agree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר knew of רב's statement. 'I didn't hear it' is a respectful way of saying he rules the other way, like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not hold this view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't take 'I did not hear it' literally. The גמרא itself explains it means 'I don't agree.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
I did not hear it,
that is to say, I do not hold of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, כְּלוֹמַר, לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's lenient view should stop us from ruling strictly.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר simply does not rule like רב.

steps.title: Maybe רב himself changed his mind: the basket story
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב retracted and agreed with שמואל, as shown by his sending doubtful birds to שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say that רב retracted and agreed with שמואל. A basket of birds with a doubtful clawing came before רב. He sent them to שמואל, who strangled them and threw them in the river. If רב had not retracted, he should have permitted them himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to רב אשי: maybe רב changed his mind. It brings a story as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב still held that a doubtful clawing is no problem, he could have just permitted the birds himself. Sending them to שמואל, who forbade them, suggests that רב now agreed with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: or if you want, say (an alternative answer)
and if it should enter your mind

phrases.english: Or if you wish, say:
Rav retracted to Shmuel's view,
for a certain basket of birds that were doubtfully clawed,
that came before Rav,
he sent them before Shmuel,
and he strangled them and threw them in the river.
phrases.notes: 'He' here is שמואל, who treated the birds as forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: And if you think he did not retract,
let him permit them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַב לְגַבֵּי דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to רב אשי's challenge, alongside אמימר's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רב retracted his lenient view and agreed with שמואל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the basket of doubtfully clawed birds that רב sent to שמואל instead of permitting it

steps.title: If רב retracted, he should have forbidden them himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the story doesn't prove a retraction, since then רב could have forbidden the birds himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, he retracted? Then let him forbid them himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the proof around and shows the story does not prove רב changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending the birds to someone else makes no sense under either view. If רב agreed with שמואל, he could have forbidden the birds himself. So the act of sending them must have some other reason.

phrases.english: Rather, what, he retracted?
Then let him forbid them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the basket story in step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Sending the birds to שמואל is equally strange if רב retracted, so it proves nothing about his opinion.

steps.title: It was שמואל's town
steps.stepSummary: רב sent the birds because the ruling belonged to שמואל in his own place, not because רב changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was שמואל's place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real reason רב sent the birds: it happened in שמואל's town, where שמואל was the authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sage does not rule against the local authority in that authority's own town. So רב may still have held his lenient view, yet he left the decision to שמואל out of respect. The proof that רב retracted falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: his place, the town where he is the halachic authority

steps.whatToRemember: The basket story does not prove רב retracted. He sent the birds out of respect, because it was שמואל's place. Practically, אמימר rules חוששין לספק דרוסה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the principle of respecting a local rav's authority (אתריה) even when you disagree with him.

phrases.english: Rather, it was Shmuel's place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basket story in a new way after step 6 showed neither reading worked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב sent the birds because of his own halachic view, either lenient or strict.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב sent them out of respect for שמואל's authority in his own town, so nothing is proven about רב's view.

steps.title: Why strangle the birds first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to strangle the birds. Why not just throw them into the river alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he need to strangle them? Let him just throw them into the river as they are!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions one detail of what שמואל did: strangling the birds before throwing them into the river. This opens a series of questions about his method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds were going to be thrown away anyway, so killing them first seems like extra work. The גמרא wants to know what the strangling added.

phrases.english: Why do I need to strangle them?
phrases.notes: This is about the birds רב sent to שמואל. שמואל strangled them and threw them into the river.

phrases.english: Let him throw them into the river as is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story of the birds sent to שמואל and examines how he got rid of them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the birds are being thrown away anyway, killing them first seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Live birds would fly away
steps.stepSummary: If they were thrown in alive, the birds would fly out of the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would fly and get away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that live birds would fly out of the water. So strangling them was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live bird that escapes could end up with a Jew who doesn't know it is forbidden and eats it. Killing it first makes sure it really disappears.

phrases.english: They fly and go away.
phrases.notes: The worry is that a Jew could later catch the bird and eat it without knowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strangling stops the birds from flying away and reaching someone who doesn't know.

steps.title: Why not wait twelve months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל didn't keep the birds for twelve months to see if they survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him keep them for twelve months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save the birds. Wait twelve months, and if they survive, they are proven not to be טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה cannot live twelve months. So waiting could have made the birds permitted, and nothing would be wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep them / wait with them
A fatally injured animal, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: And let him keep them for twelve months?
phrases.notes: If they live that long, they clearly aren't טרפה and could be permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that throwing live birds is a problem, but asks why kill them at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice to destroy the birds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waiting twelve months could clear up the doubt and save the birds.

steps.title: Keeping them could cause a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Keeping the birds around could lead someone to eat them by mistake before the time is up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could lead to a stumbling block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that keeping doubtful birds in the house is risky. Someone might forget and eat one early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twelve months is a long time. People forget which birds are under watch. Getting rid of them takes away the risk.

keyTerms.meaning: A stumbling block, a mistake that leads to sin

phrases.english: One might come to a stumbling block through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the twelve-month suggestion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting twelve months would save the birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: Waiting carries the risk that someone eats them by mistake.

steps.title: Why not sell them to non-Jews?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests selling the birds to גוים, who may eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him sell them to non-Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to avoid waste. Sell the birds to גוים, and then no Jew will stumble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling would remove the birds from Jewish homes and still bring in some money. So why destroy them?

phrases.english: And let him sell them to non-Jews?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תקלה worry by suggesting the birds leave Jewish hands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Selling to גוים removes the risk without wasting the birds.

steps.title: They might sell them back to Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גוים might resell the birds to Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would come to sell them to Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the birds could end up back with Jews through a resale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer has no reason to keep track that these birds are doubtful. So the risk would come back.

phrases.english: They would come to sell them to Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion to sell to גוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Resale brings the risk right back.

steps.title: Why the river and not the garbage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל threw the dead birds into the river instead of the garbage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him strangle them and throw them onto the garbage heap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the birds must be killed. Now it asks why the river in particular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the birds are dead, any place to throw them seems fine. So why choose the river?

phrases.english: And let him strangle them and throw them onto a garbage heap?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the strangling to the choice of the river.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dead birds don't need a river; any place would do.

steps.title: The river makes the איסור public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with 'then throw them to dogs!' and then gives the real reason: to make the איסור known.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, let's throw them to the dogs! Rather, it was to make the איסור public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first shows the question goes too far: by that logic, give them to the dogs, which would at least be useful. Then it explains that the river was chosen to publicize the איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing the birds into a river where people see it sends a public message that these birds are forbidden. The point was teaching people, not just getting rid of the birds.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל strangled the birds so they wouldn't escape, destroyed them so no one would stumble, and used the river so everyone would learn they were forbidden.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, let us throw them to the dogs!
Rather, it was to publicize the matter of the prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the garbage-heap question and ends the discussion of שמואל's method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the question proves too much, then giving the real reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any disposal place would be fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The river was chosen to publicize the איסור.

steps.title: The duck that came out of the reeds bleeding
steps.stepSummary: A duck at רב אשי's house went into the reeds and came out with blood on its neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain duck at רב אשי's house went in among the reeds and came out with its neck smeared with blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. It sets up a doubt: was the duck hurt by something that makes it a טרפה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood could come from a reed scratch, which is harmless, or from a cat's claws, which would be דרוסה and make the duck a טרפה. The next step gives רב אשי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An attack by a predator's claws, which makes an animal a טרפה

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא בַּר אֲוָוזָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: A certain duck that was in the house of רב אשי
went in between the reeds,

phrases.aramaic: נְפַק אֲתָא כִּי מְמַסְמַס קוֹעֵיהּ דְּמָא.
phrases.english: and came out with its throat smeared with blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בַּר אֲוָוזָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about doubtful טרפה birds, after the discussion of שמואל's birds ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case of doubt: a duck came out of the reeds with a bloody neck.

steps.title: רב אשי: assume a reed hurt it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי compares this to the rule about a doubt between a dog and a cat. He rules that we assume a reed hit the duck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Don't we say that if it might be a dog or might be a cat, we assume it was a dog? Here too, if it might be a reed or might be a cat, we assume a reed struck it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rules that the duck is not a טרפה. He brings the known rule that in a doubt between a dog and a cat, we assume the dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule leans toward the cause that does not make the animal a טרפה. A reed scratch is harmless, just like a dog in the known case, so the duck is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: When the injury might come from something harmless or from a predator that causes דרוסה, we assume the harmless cause, and the bird stays permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a practical way to settle a טרפה doubt. You compare it to the established dog-or-cat rule.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן סְפֵק כַּלְבָּא סְפֵק שׁוּנָרָא
phrases.english: Do we not say: if it is uncertain whether it was a dog or a cat
– I will say it was a dog?
phrases.notes: A dog's attack does not make the animal a טרפה the way a cat's claws do.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, סְפֵק קַנְיָא סְפֵק שׁוּנָרָא
phrases.english: Here too, if it is uncertain whether a reed or a cat did it
– I will say a reed struck it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָמְרִינַן סְפֵק כַּלְבָּא סְפֵק שׁוּנָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the duck case of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a doubt between a reed and a cat, we assume a reed, so the duck is not a טרפה.

steps.title: A clawed animal must be checked near the intestines
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא rule that a דרוסה must be checked in the area facing the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא said: The clawed animal that the חכמים spoke about needs to be checked in the area opposite the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling about where to check an animal that a predator clawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a דרוסה can be טרפה. This step adds a practical detail: the check is done on the flesh opposite the בני מעיים. If that flesh turned red, the predator's venom reached that area.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal clawed by a predator, whose venom may make it טרפה
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiyya said:
The clawed animal that they spoke about
needs checking opposite the intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about birds and opens a new ruling about checking a דרוסה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דרוסה must be checked in the flesh opposite the intestines.

steps.title: שמואל already said the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points out that שמואל, quoting רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, already gave the same ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The statement of the sons of רבי חייא was already explained by שמואל. שמואל said in the name of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: The clawed animal that they spoke about needs checking opposite the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows that the ruling of the sons of רבי חייא is not new, because an earlier חכם already said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the law changes here. רב יוסף traces the ruling back to an earlier source, word for word. This gives the rule an older authority and shows it was already accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: He already explained it; this was already said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא דִּבְנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא –
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: This statement of the sons of Rabbi Chiyya
Shmuel already explained it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס:
phrases.english: as Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus:
The clawed animal that they spoke about
needs checking opposite the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דִּבְנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ruling in step 18 already appears in an earlier statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same ruling was taught earlier by שמואל in the name of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

steps.title: Does clawing apply to the סימנים?
steps.stepSummary: אילפא asks whether a predator's clawing can make the סימנים a problem the way it does the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא asked: Is there a concern of דרוסה for the סימנים, or is there no concern of דרוסה for the סימנים?
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא asks a real question about how far the rule of דרוסה reaches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the venom matters near the intestines. Now the question is whether it also matters near the סימנים, the windpipe and food pipe. If it does, the check must cover that area too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised a question he was unsure about
The windpipe and food pipe, the organs cut in שחיטה
Is there or is there not; the usual shape of a two-sided question

phrases.english: Ilfa asked:
Is there clawing for the simanim,
phrases.notes: He means: can a predator's venom damage the windpipe and food pipe and make the animal טרפה?

phrases.english: or is there no clawing for the simanim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule about checking near the intestines and asks whether it also covers the סימנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the concern of דרוסה apply to the סימנים?

steps.title: The check covers the whole body cavity, even the סימנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers from רב, quoted by רב חנן בר רבא: the check covers the whole body cavity, including the סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: אילפא's question was already answered by רב חנן בר רבא. רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: The clawed animal that they spoke about needs checking opposite the entire body cavity, and even at the סימנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers אילפא's question by quoting an earlier ruling: yes, דרוסה applies to the סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling is broader than the one in step 18. The check is not only near the intestines but across the whole בית החלל. The word ואפילו ("and even") clearly includes the סימנים, which settles אילפא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: The hollow body cavity of the animal
And even; it adds a case you might have thought was left out

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָא דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא –
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: This question that Ilfa asked

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava already explained it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
The clawed animal that they spoke about needs checking
opposite the entire body cavity,
and even at the simanim.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אילפא's question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. דרוסה applies to the סימנים, because the check covers the whole body cavity, including the סימנים.

steps.title: How much must the סימנים be detached?
steps.stepSummary: אילפא asks how much of the סימנים must come loose for the animal to be טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא asked: סימנים that came loose — how much detachment makes the animal טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא asks a second question, this time about the amount of detachment. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the topic is not clawing but סימנים that pulled loose from where they belong. Everyone agrees this can make the animal טרפה. The open question is how much detachment is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Came loose; were torn away from their place

phrases.english: Ilfa asked: Simanim that came loose,
phrases.notes: He means the windpipe and food pipe pulled away from where they are attached.

phrases.english: by how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from אילפא about a different problem with the סימנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much of the סימנים must be detached to make the animal טרפה?

steps.title: Detached סימנים: once most of them are loose
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers from שמואל, quoted by רבה בר בר חנה: the animal is טרפה once most of the סימנים are detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: אילפא's question was already answered by רבה בר בר חנה. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל: סימנים that came loose make the animal טרפה when most of them came loose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא again answers אילפא by quoting an earlier ruling. The amount is רוב, the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer uses the familiar measure of רוב. A little detachment does not make the animal טרפה. Once most of the סימנים are loose, it is טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: A דרוסה must be checked across the whole body cavity, including the סימנים. סימנים that came loose make the animal טרפה once most of them are detached. In both cases, רבי זירא shows that אילפא's question was already answered by an earlier חכם.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָא דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא –
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: This question that Ilfa asked

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana already explained it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: as Rabba bar bar Chana said that Shmuel said:
Simanim that came loose — when most of them did.
phrases.notes: The words "the animal is טרפה" are left unsaid; the גמרא assumes you will add them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אילפא's question from step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal becomes טרפה once most of the סימנים are detached.

steps.title: רב אמי asks about rotting flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי asks what the law is when flesh has become rotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי asked: what is the law about rotting flesh?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי asks a new question about clawed flesh that has turned rotten. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about where and how much a clawing injury must affect the animal. Now the question is about flesh that has gone soft and rotten. Does that count as damage, and how much?

keyTerms.meaning: Rotting, flesh that has gone soft and decayed
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Ami asked:
What is the law of rotting flesh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about rotten flesh after the discussion of the סימנים in steps 20-23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the הלכה treats flesh that rotted after a clawing.

steps.title: רב already ruled that rotten flesh counts as missing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says רב יהודה already answered this in the name of רב: rotten flesh is viewed as if it is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: רב יהודה already explained רב אמי's question. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: with דרוסה, the animal is not טרפה until the flesh opposite the intestines reddens. If the flesh rotted, we view it as if it is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רב אמי's question by quoting an earlier ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives two rules. First, a clawing makes the animal טרפה once the flesh near the intestines turns red. Second, rotten flesh is treated as if it were missing. So if the animal would be טרפה without that flesh, it is also טרפה when the flesh has rotted.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal clawed by a predator
Turns red, a sign the predator's venom got in
We view it as if it is not there

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
This question that Rav Ami asked
Rav Yehuda already explained it,
for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
With a clawed animal, [it is not a treifa] until the flesh reddens
opposite the intestines;
if the flesh rotted,
we view it as if it is not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּבָעֵי רַב אַמֵּי כְּבָר פֵּירְשַׁהּ רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אמי's question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rotten flesh is treated as missing flesh. Clawing makes the animal טרפה once the flesh opposite the intestines reddens.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that rotten tissue counts as missing tissue is used right away in step 28 to declare a crumbling lung טרפה.

steps.title: What counts as rotten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far gone flesh must be to count as 'rotted'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of flesh that has 'rotted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the word 'rotted' used in רב's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said rotten flesh counts as missing, but he did not say how rotten it must be. Without a clear measure, nobody would know when to apply the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What counts as "rotted"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term in רב's rule from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact degree of rot that makes flesh count as missing.

steps.title: Rotten means flesh a doctor would scrape away
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says rotten flesh is any flesh a doctor would scrape off down to the healthy raw flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: any flesh that a doctor would scrape off, leaving only the healthy raw flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע defines 'rotted' flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is practical. If the flesh is so bad that a doctor would remove it to let healthy flesh heal, it is already as good as gone. That is why the הלכה treats it as missing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Any flesh that the doctor scrapes off
and leaves [the animal] with raw flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כֹּל שֶׁהָרוֹפֵא גּוֹרְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rotten flesh is flesh a doctor would scrape away down to the healthy raw flesh.

steps.title: A crumbling lung was declared טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells of a lung that fell apart when lifted, which they declared טרפה based on רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in the בית מדרש of רב כהנא, they brought us a lung. When it was set down it looked fine, but when it was lifted it crumbled and fell apart into pieces. We declared it טרפה based on the ruling of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells of a real case where they used the rule from steps 25-27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung looked whole while resting, but it was so rotten that it crumbled when lifted. By רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's measure, such rotten tissue counts as missing. An animal missing its lung is טרפה, so they declared this animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of a teacher
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: Rotten tissue that would crumble or be scraped away is treated as missing. This is true even if it looks whole while resting.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lung was kosher because it looked fine when set down. The test is whether it holds together, and this lung did not.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in the study hall of Rav Kahana,
they brought before us a certain lung,
that when they would set it down
it would sit nicely,
but when they would lift it up
it would crumble and fall into pieces,
and we ruled it a treifa
based on [the ruling of] Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: His rule was that flesh rotten enough to scrape away counts as missing, and an animal missing its lung is טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's definition from step 27 to a real lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung that crumbles when lifted is rotten, counts as missing, and makes the animal טרפה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a thorn wound versus clawing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says a thorn makes the animal טרפה only if it pierces into the body cavity, but clawing does so once the flesh by the intestines reddens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: With a thorn, the animal is not טרפה until the wound is pierced through to the body cavity. With דרוסה, it is טרפה once the flesh opposite the intestines reddens.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new ruling that compares two kinds of wounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thorn has no venom, so it only matters if it actually makes a hole into the body cavity. A predator's claw carries venom. So redness near the intestines is already enough, even without a hole.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
With a thorn, [it is not a treifa] until it is pierced through to the body cavity;
with clawing,
once the flesh opposite the intestines reddens [it is a treifa].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר בְּקוֹץ עַד שֶׁתִּינָּקֵב לֶחָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that compares a thorn wound with the clawing rule already given by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thorn requires piercing into the cavity. Clawing requires only reddening of the flesh opposite the intestines.

steps.title: רב זביד's version: clawing at the סימנים
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד teaches the rule differently: for the סימנים, the animal is טרפה only once the סימנים themselves redden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד taught it this way: With דרוסה, the animal is טרפה once the flesh opposite the intestines reddens. With the סימנים, it is not טרפה until the סימנים themselves redden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives a different version of רב נחמן's teaching. In his version, the clawing rule is compared with clawing at the סימנים, not with a thorn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the body, redness of the surrounding flesh near the intestines is enough. At the neck it is not enough for the flesh around the סימנים to turn red. The סימנים themselves must redden. This adds detail to steps 20-21, which said the check includes the סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way, a different version of the same teaching

steps.whatToRemember: With דרוסה, the flesh near the intestines reddening is enough. At the neck, the סימנים themselves must redden.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid taught it this way:
With clawing, once the flesh reddens
opposite the intestines [it is a treifa];
with the simanim, [it is not a treifa] until the simanim themselves redden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב נחמן's statement from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clawing at the סימנים makes the animal טרפה only when the סימנים themselves redden.

steps.title: רב ביבי בר אביי raises a new question
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי reports that רב ביבי בר אביי asked a question, which comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: רב ביבי בר אביי asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up a new question. רב פפי reports a question from רב ביבי בר אביי, and the question itself comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here. We do not yet know what is being asked. The actual question appears on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question the speaker is unsure about
An open question that has two reasonable sides

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Rav Beivai bar Abaye asked:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי בָּעֵי רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after רב זביד's version in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated. The question follows on the next amud.
